Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion

Class ConsensusGate

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.ConsensusGate
public class ConsensusGate extends Object
Arbitrates between sources that contradict each other.

A single camera reporting an absurd pose passes every individual filter: it is geometrically valid, the ambiguity is low and the robot is standing still. The only thing that gives it away is that another source says something different. That is what this class looks at.

Motion compensation

Two measurements taken dt apart describe different positions if the robot moved in between, and that is not a disagreement. Instead of propagating one pose towards the other --- which would require knowing whether the ChassisSpeeds come in robot or field frame --- the tolerance is widened by the distance the robot could have covered in that time: 
effective_tolerance = tolerance + speed * dt
It is conservative and does not depend on the reference frame. Without this, with the default 0.1 s window and a robot at 4 m/s, two perfect sources differ by 0.4 m --- comparable to the whole tolerance --- and the filter starts discarding good measurements exactly when they are needed most.

Majority vote

For each candidate, the number of others it agrees with is counted. The ones with the highest count survive. On a tie, everything in dispute is discarded: a tie means the evidence is not enough to choose, and feeding the estimator a pose another source contradicts is worse than feeding it none.
